Subject: Hosted Rate Card check + peak SLO qualification

Hi Anna — great to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can get you a firm hosted quote.

What we captured from today:
- Primary use: customer-facing delivery assistant (multi-turn chat) and nightly batch embeddings for search re-rank.
- Current prod plans: pilot in June, ramp to production in Q3.

Key numbers we need you to confirm so pricing bands are accurate:
1) Expected monthly token volume (avg): you mentioned a range — can you confirm the preferred estimate for a 12-month commit?
   - You said pilot ~10M / month, production 60–80M / month; is 75M a reasonable mid target?
2) Peak TPS / concurrency (99th pct): you reported spikes during morning syncs — what is the worst-case TPS we should design the SLA around?
3) Target $/1M tokens: do you have an internal target for unit cost (e.g., $10 / 1M tokens) or a budget band we should hit?

Attachments: I attached the MAU/token worksheet we used on the call + a quickquote template so you can see how the bands line up.
[Attachment: novacorp_mau_estimate.xlsx] [Attachment: redwood_quickquote.pdf]

Next steps I propose:
- Anna confirms the three items above (monthly token target, peak TPS, budget $/1M).
- We (Redwood) will return: 1) a 30/60/90-day hosted quickquote that maps to commit bands, 2) a recommended peak SLO and surge policy, 3) optional canary plan for Dedicated later.

If you prefer, Marissa can run a quick sensitivity table for $/1M vs. batching + KV cache impact and share it tomorrow.

Thanks — Stephanie

--

From: Anna Tan <anna.tan@novacorp.com>

Date: 2028-03-12 09:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Hosted Rate Card check + peak SLO qualification

Hi Stephanie — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Confirming the numbers from our side:

1) Monthly tokens (expected):
- Pilot (June): ~9–12M / month
- Initial production (July–Sep): 45–55M / month
- Full ramp (Oct onward): target 70–85M / month (internal target 75M is fine for planning)

2) Peak TPS / concurrency (99th):
- Observed spikes during business hours: ~160 TPS sustained for short windows (30–90s)
- Worst-case we want to design for: 250 TPS (we have a flash-burst pattern during billing cutovers)

3) Target $/1M tokens:
- Procurement target band: $7–$12 per 1M tokens depending on SLA and included support. Lower bound for proofs of value would be closer to $10 / 1M.

We also rely on low-latency for chat — 95th token latency SLO of ~150ms is ideal for user experience, but we can tolerate 250ms for brief spikes.

I'll loop in procurement for the formal budget and I attached the MAU sheet filled with our conservative ramp numbers.
[Attachment: novacorp_mau_estimate.xlsx]

—Anna
Anna Tan
Head of Product, Novacorp
anna.tan@novacorp.com | +1 (212) 555-0199
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-03-13 10:17 PDT
Subject: Fwd: Hosted Rate Card check + peak SLO qualification

Stephanie / Marissa — forwarding Anna's confirmation. Quick thoughts on pricing levers to hit that $7–$12 band:

- Batching + adaptive request coalescing: can typically reduce token billable by effective throughput improvements (depends on client QPS shape).
- KV prefix caching for the assistant: can reduce generation tokens on repeated prompts (est. 8–15% savings at 75M/month).
- Spot-capacity burst policy: offer a lower base unit cost for committed capacity and a higher on-demand rate for spikes beyond commit.

Marissa, can you run two quick quotes: 1) committed 75M/mo with 250 TPS SLO and surge policy (30% burst) targeting $9 / 1M, 2) conservative 50M/mo commit with higher burst headroom targeting $11 / 1M. Include the delta if we add 24/7 SLA and extended observability retention.

I'll draft the language for the canary + fallback policy if they want Dedicated later.

-Jordan
